_what_this_is: the explicit C1 classification of every skip predicate the automatic audit cannot prove identical between the dev box and the pod. Written after C1 attempt 5 died at the pod test gate on a predicate keyed to the SIMULATOR's AAD_SYNTHETIC_HF_TOKEN. Each entry names the machine property the predicate actually reads and how a pod decides it.
how_it_is_checked: scripts/autoinit/audit_skip_predicates.py resolves what it can from the manifest, the git index and the source, and requires every remaining predicate to appear here. A registered line that no longer holds a predicate is STALE and also fails, so this cannot rot into a list of excuses.

devbox_only_artifact.why: the premise is a gitignored artifact from an earlier experiment that C1's SetupManifest does not stage. A pod never receives it, so the test skips there by design. This is the SAME class as the two attempt-5 failures — the difference is that these ask the FILESYSTEM whether the artifact is present, so the pod and the simulation both answer correctly, while attempt 5's asked for a simulator marker the pod does not set.

pinned_snapshot_source.why: depends on the seven pinned HF dataset snapshots, which live in the host HF cache and are not staged. Already a named readiness group (renderer parity / battery source); the sweep expects these skips.

local_hf_cache.why: needs the teacher tokenizer from the local HF cache. The pod exports HF_TOKEN and can populate it; the bare dev box may not have it. Skips cleanly either way and asserts nothing about the code.

staging_premise_property.why: the repaired attempt-5 guards. They ask the filesystem for the property they need, so the dev box runs them and the pod and the simulation skip them for the same stated reason.

session_semantics.why: keyed on SESSION_KIND, which the SetupManifest sets identically in the simulation and on the pod. This is the CORRECT shape of an environment guard: the session declares it, so both agree.

manifest_derived.why: decided by the SessionSpec or by tracked source text, not by the machine, so the sweep's verdict is the pod's verdict.

machine_capability.why: needs bubblewrap, the repo venv, the canonical checkpoint and a 196-wheel vLLM wheelhouse. A rehearsal harness, not a claim about C1; it skips with the specific capability it lacks.

tests/autoinit/test_staging_contract.py:.note: the other two guards in this module (the destination-absent and nothing-undeclared premises) need NO entry: they resolve automatically to artifacts/stage1/qwen3_0p6b_init_v0/checkpoint, which C1's manifest stages, so the audit proves the premise travels.

_resolved_automatically: guards on a TRACKED logs/ record need no entry: the audit resolves the path through the module attribute that names it and finds it in the git index, so the premise provably travels in the bundle.
